acceptance.check: Members screen shows the group's invite link with Copy link as the primary action; rotate (make a new link) and disable (turn off) controls render only for the owner and are absent for a plain member.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Sign in as owner: invite URL contains the token, Copy confirms in place. Sign in as member: link visible, rotate/disable absent.

acceptance.check: Opening the invite link as a signed-in non-member shows a write-free confirm screen (so prefetch never joins); confirming joins them and lands on the group overview; confirming again leaves exactly one active membership; concurrent double-confirms yield one row; a GET-only fetch creates no row.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Integration test confirms twice plus concurrent confirms, asserts one active member row and second call is a no-op, and asserts a GET without POST writes nothing; QA opens link, confirms, lands on overview.

acceptance.check: After rotation the old token is rejected and the new token joins; after disable the token is rejected; a malformed token 404s without a query; a stale confirm POST after rotation is refused without a 500; a signed-out GET redirects to /sign-in carrying ?next=/join/<token>, honored through both sign-in and create-account; evil next values fall back to '/'.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Integration tests for rotate/disabled/malformed/stale-confirm states and evil-next fallback; QA drives signed-out open via both forms and lands on the join screen.

acceptance.check: Owner adds a placeholder by name (trimmed, 1-80 chars; blank/overlong refused); the name appears in the member list marked as placeholder with a Claim action; readMembers returns the placeholder row so the piece-4 pickers can consume it (picker rendering itself lands with piece 4, which owns the only picker).
acceptance.how_to_verify: Call add-placeholder action, assert member list contains the name with placeholder marker and Claim control; integration test asserts readMembers returns the stored name; component test asserts the marker.

acceptance.check: A signed-in member who joined through the link claims a placeholder by merge: their own row is ended and their user_id attaches to the placeholder row in one transaction, leaving exactly one active row, so everything recorded against it reads as theirs; claiming an already-claimed placeholder is refused already-claimed; a removed placeholder reports no-longer-available; an owner claim is refused (it would orphan ownership).
acceptance.how_to_verify: Integration test joins then claims, asserts one active row and reattributed records; re-claim as second user refused with row unchanged; removed placeholder distinct message; owner claim refused; QA claims in browser.

acceptance.check: Two concurrent claims on the same placeholder produce exactly one winner: one succeeds, the other is told it is already claimed and keeps their own membership untouched; nothing in any claim path 500s.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Integration test firing two concurrent claim transactions asserts one success, one conflict, winner owns the row, loser still has exactly their original active row.

acceptance.check: Join, placeholder add, claim, rotate and disable each write exactly one activity entry naming the actor in the same transaction as the change; a failed feed write rolls the change back.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Integration test asserts one entry per mutation with actor and member linkage, and feed-mock failure leaves rows unchanged.

acceptance.check: Invite block renders a static skeleton while loading (token never flashes as missing) and the copy action confirms in place with a fallback when clipboard is unavailable.
acceptance.how_to_verify: QA throttles load, asserts skeleton shape then link; clicks Copy and asserts in-place confirmation text.

alternatives_considered.approach: Separate invite_tokens table with one row per rotation instead of invite_token/invite_enabled columns on groups.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The product needs exactly one live token per group with immediate invalidation; a history table adds a second source for which token works and a join on every open, for audit value nothing reads.

alternatives_considered.approach: Claim by inserting a new member row for the claimer and repointing expense_payer/expense_share rows to it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Repointing rewrites ledger history and risks partial moves; attaching user_id to the same row reattributes everything by construction with one guarded UPDATE.

alternatives_considered.approach: Join via a POST-only Server Action with no GET route, or a join page inside the (app) group relying on requireUser().
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: IAC-2/IAC-3 require a shareable screen a signed-out person can open and be redirected from with the destination carried; no GET route has no URL to share, and inside (app) requireUser() redirects to bare /sign-in losing the destination.

alternatives_considered.approach: Claim surfaced on the join screen for signed-in non-members instead of merging on the members screen.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: IAC-4 places the Claim action on the member-list placeholder row, a member-only surface; a join-screen claim would leak placeholder names to any bearer holder and duplicate the action on two surfaces.

work_order.approach: Build invites/placeholders on the existing groups.invite_token/invite_enabled columns and nullable members.user_id with its partial unique index. Add one nullable members.display_name column used ONLY for unclaimed placeholders; reads coalesce users.displayName ?? members.display_name (live profile first). Join is an insert-select with NOT EXISTS guards decided by bare .returning() length plus same-transaction classification reads. Claim is a member-only merge in one ordered transaction: refuse owners outright; otherwise end the caller's own row first, then run the guarded attach UPDATE (WHERE user_id IS NULL); if the attach affects zero rows, restore the caller's row in the same transaction and return the typed refusal. GET /join/[token] lives OUTSIDE (app), is write-free, and the confirm is a POST Server Action; sign-in AND sign-up honor a validated next (leading single slash only). The token-keyed read returns only { id, name } for a live token. The invite block is fed by a member-scoped readInviteForMember, never by widening GroupRow. All writes go through src/lib/access.ts from Zod-validated Server Actions in one transaction with exactly one recordActivity; group.invite_* join GROUP_LIFECYCLE_KINDS. No money code touched per the binding keep-everything-else decision.
assumptions: The join URL shape /join/[token] is free to choose; no existing link format or test pins it.
New activity kinds are acceptable additions; activity.kind is free text with no DB check constraint.
Claiming is how a joined member takes a placeholder: a non-owner member merges; an owner claim is refused; a non-member cannot claim without joining first.
Claim keeps the placeholder stored name in place; claimed rows resolve the live profile name because the coalesce reads users.displayName first.
The balance precondition from piece 2 does not yet exist as code, so this plan does not enforce it on remove/leave paths.
work_order.confidence_rationale: The critique's code citations re-verified: member-only members page, bare auth cross-links, hardcoded redirectTo, union-driver returning pitfall, and both brittle fixtures are all as claimed, and the merge-design resolves the blocking contradiction with an ordering reasoned from Postgres uniqueness and the partial-index predicates. Points off because that ordering and the concurrent loser-restore path are reasoned, not integration-proven; PGlite-vs-Neon concurrency fidelity is unknown; archived-group join semantics remain unspecified.
work_order.debate_summary: Accepted eight of the ten findings and folded them in. Dismissed two: the IAC-2 confirm-screen objection (real deviation but deliberate, stated prefetch-safe engineering) and the empty-state displacement worry (member.joined already displaces Nothing here yet on every first join: existing behavior, not a regression). Neither proposal nor critique specified workable claim semantics, so the merge is the arbiter's own synthesis.
